scope: Canaccord Genuity Group Inc. (TSX:CF; not CF Industries)
currency_rule: Issuer financial statement currencies are retained. EFX and BDGI report in USD; CF reports in CAD. Quote-provider enterprise values that mix CAD market capitalization with USD issuer debt/EBITDA are rejected.

sources.source_class: primary issuer filing via SEC EDGAR
fact_extracts: Q2 revenue was US$582m versus US$615m; H1 revenue US$1,166m versus US$1,167m.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA was US$128m versus US$130m; H1 adjusted EBITDA US$265m versus US$243m.
Q2 free cash flow was US$32m and H1 free cash flow US$47m; the company-defined measure includes growth and maintenance capital, mandatory debt repayments, lease principal and disposal proceeds.
Enerflex exited Q2 with net debt of US$455m, cash of US$74m and bank-adjusted net debt/EBITDA of approximately 0.8x.
Q2 share-based compensation was US$19m versus US$3m; H1 was US$41m versus nil, largely due to the higher share price.
Q2 diluted weighted-average shares were 122.196m versus 123.401m; 122.103m common shares were outstanding on 2026-07-31.
Q2 ES backlog was US$1.453b and bookings US$488m; EI contract backlog was US$1.193b.

2026 organic capex guidance was refined to US$185m-US$195m: about US$100m growth, US$70m-US$80m maintenance, and US$15m PP&E/infrastructure. Growth capital primarily expands the US contract compression fleet.
H1 conventional CFO less PP&E/EI-asset capex was US$52m (US$121m less US$69m), versus US$44m in H1 2025; bridged with FY2025 this gives approximately US$238m LTM.
Issuer net debt excludes US$68m of current and long-term lease liabilities at 2026-06-30.
direct_passages: Generated revenue of $582 million compared to $615 million in Q2/25 and $584 million in Q1/26.
ADJUSTED EBITDA OF $128 MILLION, FREE CASH FLOW OF $32 MILLION AND RETURN ON CAPITAL EMPLOYED OF 15.4%.

Enerflex exited Q2/26 with net debt of $455 million, which included $74 million of cash and cash equivalents... Enerflex's bank-adjusted net debt-to-EBITDA ratio was approximately 0.8x at the end of Q2/26.

The Company defines free cash flow as cash provided by (used in) operating activities, less total capital expenditures... mandatory debt repayments, and lease payments, while proceeds on disposals... are added back.
Net debt is defined as total long-term debt less cash and cash equivalents, as presented in the Financial Statements.

sources.source_class: primary audited issuer filing via SEC EDGAR
fact_extracts: FY2025 revenue was US$2.571b, adjusted EBITDA US$511m, reported EBITDA US$444m, CFO US$345m, company-defined FCF US$230m, net earnings US$64m and year-end net debt US$501m.
Revenue by destination was US$1.157b United States and US$334m Canada, or about 45% and 13% of total respectively; Canadian domicile does not imply predominantly Canadian revenue.
North America produced US$1.686b of revenue and US$269m adjusted EBITDA, but this segment combines Canada and the US.
ROCE was 16.9%. The company describes EI and AMS as recurring/contracted and ES equipment sales as non-recurring.
The company had approximately 483,000 horsepower of US contract compression fleet, concentrated mostly in the Permian basin; about 20% was electric drive.
Nine of ten directors were independent; directors and officers together held approximately 0.53% of outstanding common shares.
direct_passages: Free cash flow of $230 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, also increased compared to the $222 million in the same period of 2024.

In the USA, Enerflex operates a contract compression rental fleet of approximately 483,000 horsepower as of December 31, 2025, with the largest portion operating in the Permian basin... electric drive compression representing approximately 20 percent of Enerflex's fleet.
Revenue by geographic location of customer: United States $1,157 [million]... Canada 334 [million].

sources.source_class: primary issuer releases via SEC EDGAR
fact_extracts: On October 1 Enerflex announced a contract to design, engineer, fabricate and assemble approximately 450 MW of behind-the-meter natural-gas power generation for a North American data-center developer, with deliveries in 2027-2028.

On October 13 it announced a further award of over 1 GW for a large-scale North American data-center development. Combined behind-the-meter power-generation backlog exceeded 1.75 GW, with deliveries through 2028.

Enerflex authorized approximately US$100m of ES facility/capability investment, including US$15m in 2026. The releases do not disclose customer names, contract dollars, cancellation protection, expected margins, or working-capital profile.
direct_passages: The Company has been contracted to design, engineer, fabricate, and assemble approximately 450 megawatts of behind-the-meter natural gas-fired power generation units for a North American data center developer.

Combined with additional project awards, including approximately 450 megawatts announced on October 1, 2026, Enerflex's backlog of behind-the-meter natural gas-fired power generation now exceeds 1.75 gigawatts, with deliveries extending through 2028.
Enerflex has authorized approximately $100 million of investments in its ES facilities and capabilities, $15 million of which is included in Enerflex's capital expenditure guidance for 2026.

sources.source_class: primary issuer release, MD&A and financial statements
fact_extracts: Q2 revenue was US$257.1m, up 23%; H1 revenue was US$460.4m, up 21%. Management identifies the growth as organic and attributes it to broad demand, fleet growth, utilization and pricing.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA was US$66.1m, up 25%, at 25.7% margin versus 25.3%; H1 adjusted EBITDA was US$104.2m at 22.6% margin versus 22.7%.
Revenue per truck per month rose 14% to US$47,731. Fleet count rose 8% year over year to 1,822 units.

Actual H1 CFO was US$65.3m and capex US$100.2m, implying simple CFO less capex of negative US$35.0m. Capex was US$60.2m in Q2 versus US$29.6m, reflecting more unit production, tariffs and new US service lines.
Net debt under the issuer covenant definition was US$254.1m and total debt/compliance EBITDA 1.5x. Lease liabilities were US$73.3m and are additional contractual obligations.
Q2 diluted weighted-average shares were 33.665m versus 33.769m. Q2 share-based compensation expense was US$21.5m versus US$9.2m, although derivative gains largely offset it in adjusted net income.
2026 planned capital spend was US$170m-US$200m plus US$18m-US$30m potential tariffs. A planned second US manufacturing site was not included in that range.

The service involves dangerous conditions, confined spaces, heavy equipment and possible injury/death. The AIF describes programs and board oversight, but the reviewed Q2/AIF sources did not provide a quantitative TRIR/LTIR/fatality trend, a recommendation-changing disclosure gap during rapid fleet/operator expansion.
Issuer Total Debt/net debt excludes US$73.278m of lease liabilities; lease-inclusive valuation is therefore higher than the issuer-debt EV multiple.
direct_passages: The Company achieved revenue of $257.1 million, up 23% from $208.2 million in the second quarter of 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA improved to $66.1 million, up 25% from $52.7 million in the second quarter of 2025... Revenue per truck per month was $47,731, an increase of 14%.
Cash provided by operating activities [six months]: 65,265 [US$000]; Purchase of property, plant and equipment: (100,226) [US$000].
Total Debt [at June 30, 2026]: 254,138 [US$000]... Total Debt to Compliance EBITDA was 1.5x.
Share-based compensation expense was $21.5 million compared to $9.2 million in the same quarter of the prior year.
Capital spend $170 million to $200 million; Expected potential tariffs $18 million to $30 million; Total capital spend $188 million to $230 million.
Total lease liabilities 73,278 [US$000] [at June 30, 2026].
Total Debt consists of long-term debt, less cash on hand.

sources.source_class: primary audited issuer reports and AIF
fact_extracts: FY2025 revenue was US$831.7m, up 12%; adjusted EBITDA US$198.2m, up 13%, with 23.8% margin; adjusted diluted EPS US$2.04 and reported diluted EPS US$1.75.
FY2025 actual CFO was US$163.7m and capex US$118.3m.

The company says the majority of revenue is generated in the United States but does not disclose an exact revenue split after changing to one reportable segment. At year-end, 1,368 of 1,723 trucks and 2,284 of 2,807 employees were in the US, about 79% and 81% respectively.

Badger manufactures trucks in Red Deer, Alberta and says annual production capacity exceeds 350 units; vertical integration and branch density provide scale, specification and fleet-management advantages, but the service remains locally competitive and capital intensive.
direct_passages: Adjusted EBITDA improved to $44.9 million for the quarter and $198.2 million for the year, up 2% and 13%, respectively, from 2024.
Adjusted net earnings per share was $0.34 per share for the quarter and improved to $2.04 per share for the year, up 21% from 2024.
As at December 31, 2025, Badger employed 2,284 people in the United States and 523 people in Canada... Badger's annual production capacity is more than 350 hydrovac units.
[Operational risks include] damage to or total loss of our property or assets or injury or death of our employees or of third parties.

fact_extracts: Q1 adjusted revenue was C$577.4m, up 28.8%; IFRS revenue C$573.6m, up 27.9%.
Adjusted net income attributable to common shareholders was C$39.8m and adjusted diluted EPS C$0.36 versus C$0.13; IFRS diluted EPS was C$0.08 versus a C$0.32 loss.
Wealth management revenue was C$305.1m, up 25.6%, and adjusted pre-tax income C$57.1m, up 39.9%. Client assets reached C$160.2b, up 27.9%, with acquisitions contributing to Australian growth.

Capital markets revenue was C$260.5m, up 30.2%, and adjusted pre-tax income C$37.1m versus C$5.5m. Advisory and investment-banking revenue rose sharply, but management said macro/geopolitical uncertainty limits financing visibility.
Compensation expense was 62.6% of revenue versus 60.0%, partly because share-based awards rose with the stock price.

Issued shares rose to 103.020m from 102.761m in three months. Diluted share count for IFRS EPS was 105.877m, while adjusted diluted EPS uses additional treatment for UK convertible preferred interests.
At quarter-end the employee partnership held 14.31% of common shares (15.33% as-converted), partly financed through company loans.
direct_passages: First quarter revenue of $577.4 million, an increase of 28.8% over the same period in the prior fiscal year... Diluted earnings per common share for the first fiscal quarter of $0.36.
Global wealth management operations earned quarterly revenue of $305.1 million... Total client assets... increased by 27.9% year-over-year to $160.2 billion.
Global capital markets revenue of $260.5 million improved 30.2% year-over-year... [and] contributed net income before taxes of $37.1 million.
The Employee Partnership's ownership of the Company's common shares increased from 14.18% as of March 31, 2026 to 14.31% (or 15.33% on as-converted basis) as of June 30, 2026.

sources.source_class: primary audited annual report, AIF and management circular
fact_extracts: FY2026 adjusted revenue was C$2.208b, adjusted pre-tax income C$262.8m, adjusted common net income C$133.7m and adjusted diluted EPS C$1.26 versus C$0.61. IFRS diluted EPS was a C$1.45 loss, including a C$110m US capital-markets goodwill impairment and derivative/fair-value items.
FY2026 revenue by geography was C$775.6m Canada, C$643.9m UK/Europe/Crown Dependencies, C$445.0m US and C$373.4m Australia. Canada was about 34.7% of consolidated revenue.

Wealth management revenue was C$1.123b and adjusted pre-tax income C$195.2m; capital markets revenue C$1.045b and adjusted pre-tax income C$140.9m. The two operations are economically distinct; financial-company EV/EBITDA and industrial FCF comparisons are inappropriate.

FY2026 underwriting revenue was 51% metals/mining and 13% technology; advisory revenue was 11% metals/mining and 52% technology. These are global sector shares and do not establish Canadian infrastructure or AI-attributable revenue.
Five-year adjusted diluted EPS was C$1.26, C$0.61, C$0.40, C$0.59 and C$2.51 for FY2026-FY2022, demonstrating large cycle variation.

As of March 2026 shareholders' equity was C$780.6m, including C$205.6m preferred equity; non-controlling interests were C$433.8m, bank loans C$464.5m and convertible debentures C$90.0m. Regulated capital and client settlement balances make cash-flow and net-debt shortcuts misleading.

The US capital markets unit paid US$75m of a US$80m SEC/FINRA/FinCEN settlement related to non-core trading and Bank Secrecy Act/AML compliance; US$5m remains suspended subject to a satisfactory lookback review.

The circular disclosed approximately C$79.1m of share-purchase loans and C$197.4m other insider indebtedness to the company/subsidiaries, including a C$5m forgivable executive share-purchase loan. The board later prohibited further forgivable partnership loans, but the structure creates credit/conflict risk alongside alignment.
Directors and executive officers as a group owned 10.7% of shares at 2026-03-31. CEO Dan Daviau directly held 4.007m shares plus 2.342m employee-partnership units.
direct_passages: Excluding significant items... Revenue 1,045,283 1,123,351 39,053 2,207,687 [C$000]... Earnings per common share - diluted $1.26 [for fiscal 2026].
The Company recorded a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $110.0 million related to the US cash-generating-unit.

The final settlement is $109.4 million (US$80.0 million), of which $6.8 million (US$5.0 million) is subject to suspension... As of March 31, 2026, the Company has paid $102.6 million (US$75.0 million).

Daniel Daviau 4,006,788 [Common shares]... In addition, Mr. Daviau owns 2,341,660 LP Units in the Employee Partnership.

sources.source_class: primary issuer press-release archive and issuer releases
fact_extracts: The issuer archive contained no UK wealth sale announcement, signed deal, buyer, valuation, proceeds distribution or retained-stake terms through the 2026-10-20 cutoff; its latest listed release was dated 2026-08-24.
CGWM UK agreed to acquire EFG Harris Allday front-office teams and client assets; consideration was undisclosed and completion was subject to conditions.
CF announced a C$113.5m cash redemption of all Series A preferred shares for 2026-10-01.
direct_passages: The EFG Harris Allday team is entrusted with approximately £3.1 billion in client assets and generated annual revenue of £20.3 million in the year ended December 31, 2025.
Completion of the transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to occur in the second half of calendar 2026.
The Company announced today its intention to redeem all of its outstanding... Series A... on October 1, 2026... for an aggregate amount payable to holders of $113.5 million.

sources.source_class: primary issuer releases and audited annual/interim filings
fact_extracts: CF holds about 66.9% of CGWM UK on an as-converted equity-equivalent basis; outside convertible preferred, preference and management/employee interests represent 33.1%, subject to liquidation preferences.
After the fifth anniversary, convertible preferred holders have rights to initiate a liquidity event. A management incentive plan may also pay upon such an event.
At June 2026 CGWM UK reported £23m quarterly normalized EBITDA and C$450m acquisition bank debt; whole-unit sale proceeds cannot be assigned entirely to CF common shareholders.
direct_passages: On an as converted basis and subject to the liquidation preference... the Company holds an approximate 66.9% equity equivalent interest in CGWM UK Holdco as at March 31, 2026.
After the fifth anniversary of the issuance of the Convertible Preferred Shares the holders... have certain rights in respect of initiating a liquidity event.
The total bank loans related to CGWM UK Holdco outstanding as at June 30, 2026, net of financing charges, were $450.0 million.
Normalized EBITDA... was £23.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026.

limitations: Q3 2026 releases were not yet published by the cutoff and are excluded.
No contract values, customers, expected margins or cash-conversion schedule were disclosed for EFX's October data-center awards.
BDGI no longer reports geographic segments and did not provide an exact US/Canada revenue split or quantitative worker-safety trend in the reviewed documents.
CF's adjusted results exclude numerous recurring-across-years acquisition, incentive, fair-value, legal and impairment items; both IFRS and adjusted history must be considered.
No paid analyst targets or consensus estimates were used.

No primary source through the cutoff confirms the reported UK wealth sale process, valuation, buyer, probability, proceeds waterfall or retained stake; media headlines are treated only as an unverified catalyst, not valuation evidence.
